notes: Agent read CLAUDE.md which says 'breeze testing for provider tests' — without the skill, CLAUDE.md wins.

Assertion 2 in eval 1 is weak: 'does NOT jump straight to breeze' passed for the baseline because its first step was ls/grep inspection, not breeze itself. Should be reworded to 'first test-running command is NOT breeze'.

Eval 1 tests are ALL db_test (pytestmark = pytest.mark.db_test at module level). Running with plain uv would yield 0 tests or failures without a database. The skill's uv-first guidance does not account for this — it needs a 'check for db_test marks first' instruction.

CLAUDE.md contamination: baseline agents can read CLAUDE.md which references the airflow-run-pytest skill and its uv-first recommendation. The baseline is not fully skill-naive, yet still defaulted to breeze — confirming the skill adds value.
All transcripts are planned execution only — Bash was denied in subagents. Pass rates may be inflated vs. real execution where uv would actually fail on the DB tests in eval 1.
Skill adds clear value for provider tests (eval 2): 3/3 vs 0/3 with strong evidence. Core tests (eval 1) is more nuanced due to db_test reality.
